                    ### Question
                    A 37-year-old man presents a picture of arthritis of the metacarpophalangeal of both hands and a right pleuritis. On examination, bilateral malar erythema was observed. Positive antinuclear antibodies are detected (titre 1/640), with native anti-DNA antibodies also positive; Anti-Sm negative. What would be the initial treatment of choice for this patient?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Glucocorticoids at high doses.
opb. Glucocorticoids and mycophenolate.
opc. Non-steroidal and antimalarial anti-inflammatories.
opd. The picture will probably be self-limiting and does not require treatment.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient presents with symptoms consistent with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), including arthritis, pleuritis, and bilateral malar erythema, alongside positive antinuclear antibodies and native anti-DNA antibodies. These findings confirm an active SLE diagnosis. The standard initial treatment for SLE, particularly with severe manifestations such as those exhibited by this patient, typically involves glucocorticoids. High doses are often required to manage significant symptoms effectively. Other treatment options, such as mycophenolate or antimalarials, may be considered later but are not the first-line approach in acute cases. Therefore, the most appropriate initial treatment choice is glucocorticoids at high doses.
